PROP-105g's binding rule, as literally worded ('every seeded (and later appended) entry's walletAddress value is verified... via viem's privateKeyToAccount'), is therefore not genuinely executable for Franklin, and will recur for every future Nosana-path child (REQ-202 mandates a Solana wallet for every such child). Filed as new, critical FIND-801.

Grepped the full behavioral-spec.md for 'co-located'/'coLocatedWithCoordinator' (36 matches) and read every occurrence in context. Confirmed the field is threaded consistently through REQ-105's schema/seed data (both citizens seeded true), REQ-305's append logic (always exactly false, a structural constant per REQ-301's absolute mandate), REQ-403's enumeration (citizens.filter(c => c.coLocatedWithCoordinator === true)), and the Gate section's item (11) -- with no remaining stale/implicit 'co-located' assumption anywhere in REQ-101 (whose balance lookup is walletAddress/RPC-keyed, never homeDir-dependent, confirmed at behavioral-spec.md:296-315) or REQ-402 (whose lifecycle tracking is exclusively ledger.js/active_since-keyed, confirmed at behavioral-spec.md:1694-1730) -- neither REQ references co-location at all, correctly. Separately assessed the manifest's explicit question -- whether coLocatedWithCoordinator itself needs a COORDINATOR_HOME-style canonical-constant discipline: concluded NO. Unlike HOME (which resolve-identity.mjs can source ambiguously from an explicit env object, ambient process.env.HOME, or os.homedir(), any of which could silently diverge across call sites -- exactly the hazard COORDINATOR_HOME exists to close), coLocatedWithCoordinator is NEVER computed dynamically anywhere in this spec: it is always either a fixed literal at seed time (both current citizens hardcoded true, a fact directly verified, not inferred) or a hardcoded structural constant at REQ-305 append time (always exactly false, forced by REQ-301's own absolute mandate that every spawned child is cloud-hosted). There is no multi-source-derivation hazard analogous to HOME's for this field, so a canonical-constant-export discipline is not warranted here -- a literal seed/append-time boolean is sufficiently unambiguous.

convergenceSignals.note: This is a spec review (Phase 1c), not a strict contract/sprint review -- no CRIT-XXX enumeration applies.
